newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minority party wooing Megawati - aide.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minority party wooing Megawati - aide.

text.p: Indonesia's Moslem-based minority party is lobbying Megawati Sukarnoputri, ousted leader of the rival Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), for support in its election campaign, a close aide to Megawati said on Wednesday.
The Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the PDI are battling the much-larger ruling Golkar party for May 29 general elections to the House of Representatives.

Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, is seeking to push its share of the vote to more than 70 percent from the 68 percent it won at the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
The PPP sent Mudrick Sangidoe, chief of the party branch in Solo, Central Java, to meet Megawati at her residence on Tuesday, the aide, legislator Soetardjo Soerjogoeritno told Reuters.

Sangidoe asked Megawati to allow her many loyalists in Solo to join the PPP, he said. Megawati, who was not available for comment, gave no commitment but appeared to approve the move, Soerjogoeritno said.
"The meeting should be seen in a broader scope," he said.

"What we know is the decision to send Mudrick to Megawati was made by the PPP's central executive board. The aim of the meeting is to lobby Megawati and her supporters to join the PPP in the election campaign."
PPP officials were not available for comment.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, was ousted as PDI leader by a government-backed faction last year, splitting the party into two camps.
Megawati's faction has not been allowed to contest the poll and she has asked her supporters to boycott the campaign.
Interior Minister Yogie Suardi Memet said he was aware of PPP's plan to lobby Megawati's supporters but said the move should not be given undue importance.
"It should not be dramatised (and) the campaign will continue," he told reporters before a ministerial meeting chaired by Suharto.
Memet, who did not elaborate, said the campaign would not be affected by the move, adding that it was better for Megawati's supporters to join the PPP rather than avoid the elections.
In some cities, many Megawati supporters have joined the PPP's campaign and have been seen carrying her picture. Many of her supporters have also threatened to boycott the elections.
In Jakarta, about 200 people, mostly teenagers, attended a tightly-guarded PDI campaign on Wednesday which featured supporters of the party's government-backed leader Surjadi.

More than 200 anti-riot police guarded the meeting held at a sports hall in north Jakarta. Campaign rallies organised by Surjadi's faction are always tightly guarded to prevent disturbances by Megawati's supporters.

The three legal parties are vying for votes from the electorate of 125 million to fill 425 elected seats in the 500-seat House of Representatives. The other 75 seats are alloted to the military, which does not vote.
